notes: Only the three included university-layer documents were coded (ICS 33 and ICS H32 syllabi were deferred in the collect file). Unit alignment was near complete; two A-only units (the 'absence of a single campuswide policy is intentional' sentence and the 'free to use as is or adapt' sentence) and one B-only unit (the 'basic attribution rules still apply' sentence) were real statements and kept. Main disagreements: (1) actor/phase for descriptive statements about delegation, rationale and AI limits (A: all/general, B: instructor/before-course or during-work); resolved by the passage: facts and rationales are all/general, instructions to instructors are instructor. (2) phase of the syllabus-statement requirement (before-course vs course-start); resolved as course-start. (3) policy_type: P36 vs UNCOVERED for 'explain what constitutes a violation' (kept UNCOVERED), P92 vs P17 for the ZotGPT recommendation in a single-course example (P17), P36 vs P81 for reporting to the integrity office (P81), P68 vs P37 for revise-and-resubmit (P37 with fit_note), P36 vs P28 for 'cite everything, otherwise you are likely violating' (P28), P41 vs P42 for fundamentals first (P42), P15 vs P87 and P09 vs UNCOVERED for consistent application (P87, UNCOVERED). (4) modality for imperatives in sample syllabus language (must vs should), resolved by whether the passage frames the duty as mandatory (disclosure: must; verification advice: should). (5) unit_stance: A coded require/encourage/restrict where B coded neutral; resolved to require for mandatory disclosure duties and neutral for rationales, recommendations and enforcement consequences. Topic vocabularies differed (B used its own labels); A's AGENT_BRIEF-style codes were kept.
